metadata.title: AI Coding Agents Safety Envelope - Sources
metadata.description: Official documentation and implementation references for approval systems, permission modes, permission routing, sandbox process, filesystem and network isolation, and destructive-action guards

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Documentation
official_documentation.relevance: Primary product documentation for runtime execution, approvals, and local operating model

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Permission Modes
official_documentation.relevance: All six permission modes (default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions), auto mode classifier detail, Shift+Tab cycling, disableAutoMode, plugin subagent restrictions

official_documentation.name: Anthropic Engineering: Claude Code Auto Mode
official_documentation.relevance: Deep dive on auto mode two-stage classifier architecture, transcript stripping against prompt injection, false positive/negative rates

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Hooks Documentation
official_documentation.relevance: Hook and event model for automated checks that feed approval decisions, including the `if` permission-rule scoping field on hook handlers and its fail-open behavior

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Permissions Reference
official_documentation.relevance: Full permission rule syntax: evaluation order (deny > ask > allow, first match wins), tool-name and parameter-value (`Tool(param:value)`) rules, Agent/MCP/Read/Edit/WebFetch/Cd specifiers, protected paths, managed-only settings, and settings precedence for permission rules

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Settings Documentation
official_documentation.relevance: Settings precedence order (managed > CLI args > local project > shared project > user) that permission-rule audits must reason about alongside deny-wins-regardless-of-scope semantics

official_documentation.name: Claude Code — Configure the sandboxed Bash tool
official_documentation.relevance: Primary source for the shipping Bash sandbox: settings.json keys, mode names, platform backends, credential deny/mask, TLS-blind allowlist caveat, and documented compatibility failures.

official_documentation.name: OpenAI Codex — Sandboxing concept doc
official_documentation.relevance: Primary source for Codex sandbox mode names (read-only/workspace-write/danger-full-access) and the separate approval-policy axis (look up the current approval values).

implementation_references.name: Claude Code GitHub Repository
implementation_references.relevance: Closed-source product page and issue tracker; not the implementation source — use code.claude.com/docs/en for authoritative behavior docs

implementation_references.name: Anthropic: Building Effective Agents
implementation_references.relevance: High-level guidance on agent control boundaries and reliable tool use

implementation_references.name: OpenAI Codex Core Sandbox Support Matrix
implementation_references.relevance: Pinned first-party source for macOS Seatbelt, Linux Landlock/bubblewrap, Windows sandbox backend, split policy fallback, and fail-closed behavior

implementation_references.name: OpenAI: Building a safe, effective sandbox to enable Codex on Windows
implementation_references.relevance: May 2026 first-party explanation of sandbox design tradeoffs, useful defaults, full-access risk, and process-tree enforcement

cross_runtime_references.name: Codex CLI Repository
cross_runtime_references.relevance: Cross-runtime comparison point for command execution, approvals, and sandbox boundaries

cross_runtime_references.name: OpenAI Codex Split Permissions Source
cross_runtime_references.relevance: First-party source for split filesystem policy, read/write/deny access, network policy, protected metadata names, and sandbox capability modeling. Prefer `main` over a pinned commit for this fast-moving config surface

cross_runtime_references.name: OpenAI Codex Execpolicy README
cross_runtime_references.relevance: First-party source for prefix-rule policy evaluation, strictest-decision wins, examples as tests, host_executable matching, and structured policy output.

cross_runtime_references.name: OpenAI Codex Network Proxy Config Source
cross_runtime_references.relevance: First-party source for domain allow/deny config, local binding policy, unix socket permissions, and MITM proxy settings

cross_runtime_references.name: OpenAI Codex Network Connect Policy Source
cross_runtime_references.relevance: First-party source for network destination checks, deny precedence, loopback/private target handling, and local binding enforcement

cross_runtime_references.name: Model Context Protocol Specification
cross_runtime_references.relevance: Reference for tool and server capability boundaries when execution crosses process or transport layers

security_references.name: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
security_references.relevance: Useful security baseline for least privilege, environment separation, and command execution boundaries

security_references.name: OWASP Docker Security Cheat Sheet
security_references.relevance: Practical isolation patterns when coding-agent execution uses containers or microVMs

goose_aaif_references.name: Goose moves to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
goose_aaif_references.relevance: April 7, 2026 post documenting transfer of goose from Block to AAIF (Linux Foundation). Repository moved to aaif-goose/goose, documentation to goose-docs.ai.

goose_aaif_references.name: OpenTelemetry GenAI Agent Spans Semantic Conventions
goose_aaif_references.relevance: Experimental OTel spec for gen_ai agent spans: gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.agent.name/id/version, tool child spans gen_ai.tool.name / gen_ai.tool.call.id. Relevant to sandbox denial events and agent-span observability.
